title: Logit baselines sit further from zero on no-op edits

deviations_from_draft_spec: Draft said the arrow reads '6.2x' from BL1_easy. The run's own file declares ratio_bl1_over_activation = 7.234 with ratio_basis = BL1_hard / median(activation-class medians). The figure draws 7.2x from BL1_hard, the ratio the artifact actually reports. (0.150/0.0241 = 6.23 is the BL1_easy ratio, which the artifact does not headline.)

Draft asked for IQR error bars on every bar. Only the activation class is a class of many readouts (n=19), so only it carries an IQR. The four BL1 entries are single readouts and are drawn without error bars.

caption: Median displacement on 15 no-op edit pairs, in units of each readout's own bootstrap null SD. The four logit-only baseline variants (orange) sit 0.092-0.178 null SD from zero; the 19 activation-class readouts have a class median of 0.024 null SD (blue bar, whisker = interquartile range across the 19 readouts). The artifact's headline ratio, BL1_hard over the activation-class median, is 7.2x. Larger no-op displacement is what drives the logit baselines' higher no-op false-alarm counts (5-8 of 15 pairs with a CI excluding zero, versus 0-3 of 15 for activation readouts); no-op edits are not bitwise identical at the activation level, so activation readouts move too, only far less.
